newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower, weak cash hits August.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower, weak cash hits August.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Wednesday, led by August on weak cash basis levels which suggested waning demand for old crop, traders said.

"We have had a pretty aggressive bean rally but the bids in the country didn't reflect it so it's just a realignment," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp. "Part of it is, we're coming up to first notice day."

Cash soybean basis levels fell sharply early Wednesday and soymeal offers were also lower. Merchandisers pointed to increased farmer selling. They also noted end-users were willing to wait for cheaper new crop supplies.
Trade sources expected soybean registrations posted against the August would total less than 500,000 bushels on Thursday, first notice day for deliveries.

New crop months ended a shade lower, dragged down by August. Conflicting weather reports also encouraged long liquidation, traders said. There was talk that some meteorologists had increased predicted rainfall amounts in their midday updates but traders said most forecasters still expected only scattered showers this weekend.
Soybeans ended 10-1/2 to 1/2 cent per bushel lower with August down 10-1/2 at $7.56-1/2.

New crop months had opened higher amid ongoing concerns persistent dry weather would stress soybeans. Traders said August was the critical weather month for soybeans because that is when most of the plants bloom and set pods. Stress during that period can cut the number of pods and thus trim yield, they said.
"Corn is made in July but soybeans are made in August," a trader said.

On the day, commercials were largely sellers of November, an indication of hedge activity, traders said. Farmers Commodities Corp sold 3.5 million bushels November while Cargill Inc and ADM each sold 2.5 million November.
Refco Inc sold three million November but bought at least 2.5 million. E.D. and F. Man International and LIT each sold 2.5 million November.

Traders said there were at least one million bushels August sold on sell stops when that contract fell sharply near midday. Cargill Inc sold at least 700,000 August and Temco Inc sold 1.5 million August.
In spread action, Smith Barney bear spread one milion bushels November/September at 37-1/2 cents, premium September.
In options, Smith Barney sold 400 September $8.00 calls at one cent and Tradelink bought 150 November $6.50 calls at 26 cents, pit sources said.
Volatility in the November was pegged at 27 percent, up from Tuesday's 25 percent.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 82,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 64,865. Options volume was pegged at 20,000 contracts, against Tuesday's 25,695.
